content:
Factors, multiples, primes and divisibility rules are classic Class 4 Olympiad scoring territory — quick marks if the rules are cold. Here is what the IMO Class 4 factors and multiples chapter tests, the facts to drill, the traps, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 4 Maths Olympiad Factors and Multiples chapter tests

  • Factors and multiples of a number
  • Prime and composite numbers
  • Divisibility rules for 2, 3, 5, 9 and 10
  • HCF and LCM basics

Key facts your child should know

  • A prime has exactly two factors; 1 is neither prime nor composite; 2 is the only even prime.
  • Factors are finite; multiples never end.
  • Divisible by 3 ⇔ digit sum divisible by 3; by 9 ⇔ digit sum divisible by 9.
  • HCF(12, 18) = 6; LCM(4, 6) = 12.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Calling 1 a prime number.
  • Missing a factor when counting them all.
  • Mixing up HCF and LCM in word problems.

quiz.title: IMO Class 4 Factors and Multiples Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: IMO Maths Olympiad Class 4: Factors and Multiples

questions.q: Which of these shows 72 as a product of prime factors?
questions.explanation: Dividing by primes step by step: 72 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. Every factor in this product is prime and the product equals 72.

questions.q: Mira claims all of 60, 84, 106, 132 are multiples of 12. Which number proves her wrong?
questions.explanation: 60 = 12 × 5, 84 = 12 × 7, 132 = 12 × 11, but 106 ÷ 12 = 8 remainder 10, so 106 is not a multiple of 12.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a multiple of 8: 48, 72, 84, 96?
questions.explanation: 48 = 8 × 6, 72 = 8 × 9, 96 = 8 × 12, but 84 ÷ 8 = 10 remainder 4, so 84 is not a multiple of 8.

questions.q: How many prime numbers are there from 1 to 20?
questions.explanation: The primes here are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19 — 8 in all.

questions.q: What is the HCF of the three numbers 12, 18 and 30?
questions.explanation: Common factors of 12, 18 and 30 are 1, 2, 3, 6. The greatest of these is 6.

questions.q: What is the third common multiple of 5 and 10?
questions.explanation: Common multiples of 5 and 10 are 10, 20, 30, … The third one is 30.

questions.q: Count the numbers that are factors of BOTH 20 and 36. How many are there?
questions.explanation: The common factors of 20 and 36 are exactly the factors of their HCF 4: 1, 2, 4 — 3 numbers.

questions.q: Rina lists all the factors of 64 and crosses out 64. What is the biggest factor left in her list?
questions.explanation: Factors of 64: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64. Leaving out 64 itself, the largest one is 32 (it equals 64 ÷ 2).

questions.q: Which is the largest multiple of 6 that is less than 100?
questions.explanation: 6 × 16 = 96, while 6 × 17 = 102 crosses 100. So the answer is 96.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a factor of 90?
questions.explanation: 90 ÷ 9 = 10, 90 ÷ 15 = 6, 90 ÷ 18 = 5 — all exact. But 90 ÷ 12 does not give a whole number, so 12 is not a factor.

faq.q: Why is 1 not a prime number?
faq.a: A prime needs exactly two different factors. The number 1 has only one factor (itself), so it is neither prime nor composite.

faq.q: What is the divisibility rule for 9?
faq.a: Add the digits; if the sum divides by 9, so does the number. 729 → 7+2+9 = 18 → divisible.
